title: Cerebral Palsy
Programme
hero.text: For children and adults living with cerebral palsy, to improve mobility, build muscle strength and support overall wellbeing using the Kozyavkin Method - introduced for the first time in the GCC at Cambridge Hospital.

overview: Cerebral palsy is a non-progressive neurological disorder caused by damage to the brain before, during or shortly after birth. Although the initial brain injury does not worsen over time, its effects can evolve as a child grows, affecting movement, muscle structure, coordination and internal organ function.

Our specialised cerebral palsy programme provides comprehensive management and tailored intervention, enhancing mobility, improving muscle strength and promoting overall wellbeing, so every patient can work towards their fullest potential.

topics.label: What Is the Cerebral Palsy Programme?

blocks.text: Our cerebral palsy programme brings together a multidisciplinary rehabilitation team and specialised therapies tailored to each patient’s condition and needs. Treatment focuses on improving movement and physical function, reducing muscle stiffness, building strength and coordination, and developing greater independence in daily life.

Cambridge Hospital is the only provider in the GCC to introduce the Kozyavkin Method - an internationally recognised, intensive neurorehabilitation programme for cerebral palsy and other neurological conditions where increased muscle tone and spasticity affect movement.

Developed by Professor Kozyavkin, it has a clear goal: to improve quality of life for every patient living with neurological disorders. Delivered through intensive cycles of therapy, it complements traditional therapies by helping manage muscle tone and spasticity, improve joint movement and control, and support tissue health through increased blood flow, helping each patient work towards their motor milestones and greater functional ability.
Cerebral palsy is the most common condition treated, but the Kozyavkin Method can benefit a range of neurological and musculoskeletal conditions, including:

items: Cerebral palsy in all its forms, including quadriplegia, spastic diplegia, double hemiplegia, hemiplegia, hemiparesis, paraparesis, and atonic, astatic, mixed and hyperkinetic forms
Delayed motor development in young children
Effects of traumatic brain injury and residual effects of cerebrovascular lesions and CNS infections
Osteochondrosis and spondylosis with severe muscular tonic syndromes
Secondary vertebral conditions and non-inflammatory peripheral joint diseases (in remission)
Diseases of the peripheral nervous system (in remission)

blocks.text: Care is tailored to each patient and may include:

items: Teaching coping mechanisms and self-management skills

topics.label: How Cerebral Palsy Affects the Body

blocks.text: Cerebral palsy affects posture, movement and coordination. As a child grows, muscles can shorten and tighten and muscle tone can increase, which can give the impression that the condition is worsening. Children may also experience developmental delays.

Cerebral palsy can also affect proprioception - the body’s ‘automatic’ ability to sense its position, balance and movement through receptors in the joints, tendons and muscles. This sense is vital for coordinating everyday movements and learning new ones.
That’s why effective, lifelong management matters - and why the Kozyavkin Method addresses not only the peripheral muscles and joints but also re-educates movement and the musculature of the spine.

As part of our commitment to bringing worldleading rehabilitation to the UAE, Cambridge Hospital is the first and only centre in the country licensed to provide the Kozyavkin Method - an internationally recognised intensive neurorehabilitation system proven to improve motor function, reduce spasticity, and enhance overall quality of life for patients with cerebral palsy.

Our multidisciplinary team, including physiotherapists, occupational therapists and speech and language therapists, creates tailored plans that enhance mobility, coordination and physical function through intensive, evidence-based rehabilitation.

We emphasise early intervention, work closely with families and use advanced, engaging technology, including therapeutic games and interactive exercises, to motivate patients while promoting the neuroplasticity essential to recovery. We monitor progress closely and adjust each plan as needed.
